hook: The Okefenokee Swamp is the largest blackwater swamp and freshwater ecosystem in North America today.

sections.voiceover: The Okefenokee Swamp is the largest blackwater swamp and freshwater ecosystem in North America today.

In July 2026, the Okefenokee Swamp officially joined the UNESCO World Heritage List. This sprawling ecosystem spans across southeastern Georgia and into parts of northeastern Florida. Which U.S. site is it?
It marks the 27th U.S. site, but it stands out for its management.
The Okefenokee National Wildlife Refuge is the first site managed entirely by the U.S. National Wildlife Refuge System. It remains the biggest freshwater ecosystem in North America.
The swamp now stands as Georgia's first official UNESCO site.
